name: LinkedIn Ads
verdict: Development tier needs access approval, and serving many customers needs the Standard tier through a support ticket with a demo video. LinkedIn picks partners at its discretion, with no published timeline (6-12+ weeks is an inference).
needGuide: Yes — apply for Advertising API access and plan the Standard-tier video request; nothing scales until approved.

auth.detail: 3-legged authorization-code OAuth only (client credentials is not available for marketing use). Access tokens last 60 days; programmatic refresh tokens are limited to a small set of partners; PKCE is not documented. Members must accept all requested scopes together.

effort.timeToFirstTest: days to weeks (Development tier needs approval; timeline not documented)
effort.timeToProduction: unknown; likely 6-12+ weeks (inference, no published timeline)

approval.gate: Advertising API starts in the Development tier after an access application: you can edit at most 5 ad accounts you administer, create 1 test ad account via API, and real accounts must be made in Campaign Manager. Serving many customers needs the Standard tier, requested by a support ticket on the Developer Support Portal with a video showing the platform creating, editing or optimizing LinkedIn campaigns. LinkedIn selects partners at its discretion and may decline even qualifying ones; no timeline is published.

scopes.why: Scopes (r_ads, rw_ads, r_ads_reporting…) come with each approved API product, and members also need the matching role.
scopes.summary: r_ads, rw_ads, r_ads_reporting for advertising; rw_organization_admin and r_organization_admin for Page admin data; w_organization_social and r_organization_social for Page posts. Scopes are granted automatically once API access is approved; the member also needs the matching role.

prerequisites: Account and owner: Someone who can create a developer app tied to the company's LinkedIn Page; the Page admin must approve the association and verification (likely via a verification link in the app Settings, not confirmed on the pages read). Use a company-owned LinkedIn login.

Where you register: Developer Portal -> Create app (associate a LinkedIn Page) -> Products tab -> Advertising API -> Request access (access form); ad accounts: Products -> View Ad Accounts -> Add Ad Account

registerAt.path: Developer Portal -> Create app (associate a LinkedIn Page) -> Products tab -> Advertising API -> Request access (access form); ad accounts: Products -> View Ad Accounts -> Add Ad Account

steps.do: Create or confirm a LinkedIn Company Page; Page super admin available
Create the app at linkedin.com/developers/apps/new and associate it with the Page; have the Page admin verify it
Read the restricted use-cases list, then Products tab -> Advertising API -> request access and complete the form
After approval, Products -> View Ad Accounts -> Add Ad Account (9-digit ID from Campaign Manager); generate a test token
Build 3-legged OAuth (authorization at /oauth/v2/authorization, tokens at /oauth/v2/accessToken); handle 60-day expiry with re-auth
Record a demo video of the platform creating, editing and optimizing campaigns on LinkedIn
Submit Standard tier upgrade ticket at linkedin.com/help/linkedin/ask/dsapi; follow up through support
Use current versioned API; version 202511 sunsets 2026-11-16

roles.team: Someone who can create a developer app tied to the company's LinkedIn Page; the Page admin must approve the association and verification (likely via a verification link in the app Settings, not confirmed on the pages read). Use a company-owned LinkedIn login.
roles.console: none documented in the sources read; the Developer Portal app likely has a team members area (unconfirmed).
roles.customer: A member holding a role on the ad account (rw_ads needs ACCOUNT_BILLING_ADMIN, ACCOUNT_MANAGER, CAMPAIGN_MANAGER or CREATIVE_MANAGER) or on the Company Page; their token fails without the role. A Company Page can link many ad accounts, but an ad account links to only one Page, permanently.

testing: Development tier: Token Generator in the Developer Portal (or the Postman workspace); map up to 5 ad accounts you administer; 1 API-created test ad account.
Customer ad accounts beyond those cannot be used until Standard.

blockers.problem: Development tier caps at 5 editable ad accounts
blockers.fix: A multi-customer agent cannot launch until Standard is approved.

blockers.problem: Standard is discretionary with no published timeline or criteria
blockers.fix: Plan for ticket follow-ups and a polished demo video.

blockers.problem: Token from a member without a role on the Page or ad account returns errors
60-day access tokens and no standard refresh tokens mean customers must re-authorize periodically unless you are a partner with programmatic refresh

automation.agentCan: Draft the access-form use case and Standard upgrade narrative, write the OAuth and role-check code, script the demo flow, run API test calls with the generated token, migrate to the current API version.
automation.humanMust: Page admin verification, LinkedIn login and 2FA, submitting the access form and support ticket, recording the demo video, communicating with LinkedIn support.

uncertain: Company Page verification steps, Development-tier approval time and Standard review time were not documented in the fetched pages; the increasing-access page without a version parameter errored; no community sources were checked because search and fetch budgets ran out.
